title: Collections Framework: List, Set, Queue & PriorityQueue
subtitle: Explore the internal mechanics of ArrayList 1.5x dynamic growth, LinkedList node pointers, HashSet dummy values, ArrayDeque circular ring buffers, and PriorityQueue binary min-heap sift operations.
mentalModel: Choose ArrayList for fast random access (O(1)) and CPU cache locality; ArrayDeque for high-throughput LIFO/FIFO queues without node allocations; PriorityQueue for O(log N) prioritized job scheduling; HashSet for O(1) unique key filtering.

failureModes: ConcurrentModificationException with Iterator: Mutating a collection directly via `list.add()` while iterating with a foreach loop violates the fail-fast `modCount` invariant. Use `iterator.remove()` or `ConcurrentHashMap` instead.
Unbounded ArrayList Growth: Continuously adding millions of elements without pre-sizing the initial capacity triggers frequent array reallocations and GC memory copy spikes.
tradeOffs: ArrayList vs LinkedList: ArrayList has O(1) random index access and contiguous CPU cache locality. LinkedList has O(1) insertion at ends but suffers 40 bytes per node memory overhead and cache misses.
theoryData.productionScenario: In low-latency payment processing pipelines, replacing legacy `java.util.LinkedList` and `java.util.Stack` with `java.util.ArrayDeque` reduced GC pressure by 40% due to eliminating millions of transient Node object heap allocations.

interviewQA.q: Why does ArrayDeque outperform LinkedList for Queue and Stack use cases?
interviewQA.a: 1) ArrayDeque is backed by a contiguous circular array, which has excellent CPU cache locality and generates zero node allocations during push/pop. 2) LinkedList allocates a 40-byte Node object for every single element, causing memory fragmentation and GC overhead.

interviewQA.q: How does PriorityQueue implement a Min-Heap without using explicit tree node pointers?
interviewQA.a: It uses an array representation of a complete binary tree where for an element at index k: Parent is at (k - 1) >>> 1, Left child is at 2*k + 1, and Right child is at 2*k + 2. Insertion uses siftUp() and removal of the root uses siftDown(), maintaining the heap property in O(log N) time.

quizData.question: What is the growth formula for an ArrayList when its capacity is exceeded in OpenJDK?
quizData.answer: oldCapacity + (oldCapacity >> 1), which equals approximately 1.5x the previous capacity.

quizData.question: Does HashSet allow duplicate elements or multiple null values?
quizData.answer: No duplicates are allowed. HashSet permits at most ONE null value (stored at bucket 0 of the underlying HashMap).
